Tool Name: ARSENAL LAB - Applied Hardware Attacks: Prototyping Malicious Hardware on the Cheap
Description: Multi-million-dollar hardware attacks might catch headlines, but the reality is that custom crafting your own malicious hardware is cheaper and easier than ever. We'll have all the tools you need set up and ready to go to prototype, build, and test a custom hardware implant. Based on your time and experience, you'll have the opportunity to walk through 4 hands-on stages of hardware implant design: Stage 1: Analysis: We'll have an off-the-shelf embedded system system for you to poke around at and figure out how to escalate privilege. Stage 2: Prototyping: Next, you'll walk through the process of modifying a few lines of code to turn a microcontroller into a standalone payload delivery device. Stage 3: Interfacing: You'll put your devlcie to the test - hook it up to the target system, and see if our payload delivers successfully. Stage 4: Customization: We can walk through the process of designing and milling a circuit board to adapt our device to a different target system. You can try your hands a one or all of the stages. On the software side, you'll interact with an embedded linux shell, modify some C code, and work with circuit board CAD tools. On the hardware side, you'll flash a microcontroller, wire it to a target system, and if time permits, mill a custom circuit board. In the end, you'll get to take home your own customized malicious hardware device. Hopefully you'll walk away with a few new skills and a better appreciation of what's possible with just a little hardware experience.
